_note: Core/Device (parity/F06-device.md), the FIELD MATRIX. Every action's fields, their type, and which renderers can legitimately answer them. This is the executable form of the module's central promise: a field the platform cannot answer is ABSENT, never 0, "", false or an invented value, so a caller checks for the key rather than for a falsy value (durability P4, typed absence). A runner asserts three things per row: the field is present on every renderer listed in `on`, it is absent on every renderer not listed, and where it is present it carries the declared type. `always` means present on all three.
_runner: No runner is wired yet (registration is in the F06 handoff).

brand._note: web only when userAgentData names one

model._note: the PLATFORM's own answer and deliberately not normalized: Android returns the marketing name (Pixel 8), iOS the family (iPhone), because iOS exposes no marketing name and a hand-kept table of them is wrong the week a phone launches

modelId._note: the machine id. Android has no such concept and answers designName instead

isDevice._note: a browser cannot know it is not an emulator

totalMemory._note: web only where navigator.deviceMemory exists, and then it is a coarse GB bucket

isRooted._note: a HINT. Mandatory/Security owns the real posture

installTime._note: exact on Android (PackageInfo), derived on iOS (the Documents directory's creation date), and on the web it is when this browser profile first ran the app

installReferrer._note: needs the Play Install Referrer library, which this module deliberately does not depend on. Absent everywhere until an app adds it

installationId._note: a random UUID, never derived from hardware. Survives a reinstall on iOS (keychain) and does not on Android (app container): platform truth, documented, not smoothed over. Absent when generate_installation_id is off

previousVersion._note: absent on a first install, present for the life of an upgraded install

cornerRadius._note: Android needs API 31; absent below that, never guessed

hasDynamicIsland._note: always false off iOS. The field exists so one question works everywhere

currency._note: Intl exposes no locale to currency mapping, so the web omits it

level._note: absent wherever there is no readable battery, including a browser that removed the API

lowPowerMode._note: always false on the web: no API, and every caller branches on it

capabilities._note: Ten plain booleans rather than ten optionals: a capability check that can be null is a capability check nobody writes. false means not present OR not detectable from here, and the module README says which is which per platform. This answers PRESENCE, never permission.

context._note: The nine reactive vars, their defaults, and what publishes them. `orientation` is a PLAIN READ: Core/Orientation owns locking and the claim stack, and this module never writes orientation.
